 A cold front moving across Southwest Florida Saturday evening will bring scattered showers and a few thunderstorms before conditions turn drier and breezier overnight.
 Showers and storms will gradually shift south with the front, with most activity expected to wrap up by around 9 to 10 p.m. Saturday. Behind the front, drier air will move into the region, bringing lower humidity and a stretch of mostly sunny weather through much of the upcoming week.
 Why will it be so windy?
 The biggest impact from this front will be the prolonged stretch of gusty northeast winds.
 A developing area of low pressure off the Carolinas, combined with strong high pressure building behind the front, will create a tight pressure gradient across the eastern United States and Florida. That pressure difference will cause air to move more quickly, producing persistent breezy to windy conditions across Southwest Florida.
 Northeast winds will increase Sunday, with sustained speeds generally between 15 and 25 mph and gusts reaching 30 to 35 mph in spots. The strongest gusts are expected along the coast and in exposed areas.
 Winds will remain elevated into Monday before gradually easing through the middle and latter part of the week.
 Cooler mornings and comfortable afternoons
 Behind the front, temperatures will trend several degrees below seasonal averages, especially during the overnight and early morning hours.
 Sunday morning temperatures will range from the middle 60s inland to around 70 degrees near the coast. Afternoon highs will reach the lower to middle 80s, with the persistent breeze making it feel cooler at times.
 Morning lows will dip into the middle 60s across much of the area early next week, with a few inland locations potentially reaching the lower to middle 60s. Afternoon highs will generally remain in the lower to middle 80s through the 10-day forecast.
 For reference, the normal high in Fort Myers is around 87 degrees, while the normal low is near 69 degrees.
 Rain chances will be limited after Saturday night, with mostly sunny to partly cloudy skies expected through much of next week. Lower humidity will also make conditions feel more comfortable compared with recent days.
 Small craft advisory and rough Gulf waters
 Boaters should prepare for hazardous conditions as northeast winds strengthen over the Gulf of America.
 A Small Craft Advisory is in effect from 5 p.m. Saturday through 3 a.m. Tuesday for portions of Tampa Bay, Charlotte Harbor, Pine Island Sound and the coastal waters from Tarpon Springs to Bonita Beach.
 Offshore, northeast winds of 20 to 30 knots, with gusts up to 35 knots, and seas of 6 to 13 feet are expected in the advisory area.
 Wave heights closer to shore will also be elevated, with 3- to 5-foot seas possible Monday and Tuesday before gradually subsiding. Conditions will remain rough in bays and other exposed waterways as well.
 These conditions can make boating dangerous, particularly for smaller vessels. Boaters should check the latest marine forecast and heed any advisories before heading out.
 Beachgoers should also use caution around rough surf and changing water conditions.
 A developing low off the East Coast
 The same broad weather pattern responsible for the windy conditions in Florida will also support the development of a strong non-tropical low-pressure system off the East Coast.
 The National Hurricane Center says the system could develop subtropical characteristics as it moves slowly and erratically offshore through the middle of next week. As of Saturday evening, the chance of tropical or subtropical development is near 0% over the next 48 hours and 20% over the next seven days.
 Regardless of whether the system becomes subtropical, it could bring high winds, dangerous surf and coastal flooding to portions of the U.S. East Coast.
 The system is expected to remain well away from Southwest Florida, but its interaction with high pressure to the north will help maintain the tight pressure gradient and gusty northeast winds across our area.
